--- title: "SQL Project" --- ## Github Repo [Github Repo](https://github.com/ADC-405-S26/Project_2_SQL_Team_7) ## Intro This project was focused on using SQL to query database data. My project partner Nick Katz and I focused on force plate jumping metrics. We created our own database using data from three different types of jumps. After created the database we used SQL code to make queries to extract data from the database to create visualizations to compare said data. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cat("Working directory:", getwd(), "\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Working directory: /cloud/project/sql_project ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat("CMJ exists:", file.exists("CMJ_Data.csv"), "\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` CMJ exists: TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat("CMJ in subfolder exists:", file.exists("sql_project/CMJ_Data.csv"), "\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` CMJ in subfolder exists: FALSE ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} SHOW TABLES; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS CMJ_cleaned; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS MR_cleaned; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS SJ_cleaned; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS athletes; ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} CREATE TABLE athletes ( athlete_id VARCHAR(255) PRIMARY KEY, athlete_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL); ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} COPY athletes FROM 'athletes.csv' (FORMAT CSV, HEADER, NULL 'NA'); SELECT * FROM athletes LIMIT 5; ```

The dataset also has a metric (jump_height) to compare performance. ::: {.cell output.var='Left_Right_combined'} ```{.sql .cell-code} SELECT a.athlete_name, a.athlete_id, sj.jump_height, sj.sj_right_avg_propulsive_force_n, sj.sj_right_avg_landing_force_n, sj.sj_right_force_at_peak_landing_force_n, sj.sj_right_force_at_peak_propulsive_force_n, cmj.cmj_left_avg_propulsive_force_n, cmj.cmj_left_avg_landing_force_n, cmj.cmj_left_force_at_peak_propulsive_force_n, cmj.cmj_left_force_at_peak_landing_force_n, sj.sj_left_avg_propulsive_force_n, sj.sj_left_avg_landing_force_n, sj.sj_left_force_at_peak_landing_force_n, sj.sj_left_force_at_peak_propulsive_force_n FROM athletes AS a LEFT JOIN ( SELECT athlete_name, athlete_id, AVG(right_avg_propulsive_force_n) AS cmj_right_avg_propulsive_force_n, AVG(right_avg_landing_force_n) AS cmj_right_avg_landing_force_n, AVG(right_force_at_peak_propulsive_force_n) AS cmj_right_force_at_peak_propulsive_force_n, AVG(right_force_at_peak_landing_force_n) AS cmj_right_force_at_peak_landing_force_n, AVG(left_avg_propulsive_force_n) AS cmj_left_avg_propulsive_force_n, AVG(left_avg_landing_force_n) AS cmj_left_avg_landing_force_n, AVG(left_force_at_peak_propulsive_force_n) AS cmj_left_force_at_peak_propulsive_force_n, AVG(left_force_at_peak_landing_force_n) AS cmj_left_force_at_peak_landing_force_n FROM CMJ_cleaned GROUP BY athlete_id, athlete_name) AS cmj ON a.athlete_id = cmj.athlete_id LEFT JOIN( SELECT athlete_name, athlete_id, AVG(right_avg_propulsive_force_n) AS sj_right_avg_propulsive_force_n, AVG(right_avg_landing_force_n) AS sj_right_avg_landing_force_n, AVG(right_force_at_peak_propulsive_force_n) AS sj_right_force_at_peak_propulsive_force_n, AVG(right_force_at_peak_landing_force_n) AS sj_right_force_at_peak_landing_force_n, AVG(left_avg_propulsive_force_n) AS sj_left_avg_propulsive_force_n, AVG(left_avg_landing_force_n) AS jump_height_m AS jump_height FROM SJ_cleaned GROUP BY athlete_id, athlete_name, jump_height) AS sj ON a.athlete_id = sj.athlete_id WHERE cmj.athlete_id IS NOT NULL AND sj.athlete_id IS NOT NULL; ``` average propulsive force of the right leg of an athlete compared to the left leg. The second visualization shows the peak propulsive force of the right leg compared tot he left leg. As expected there is a strong correlation between the left and right leg for most athletes. Interestingly, there are several athletes who have both a great left and right leg propulsion, and they sit close tot he top on both, but for some reason they have a lower jump height, which doesn't make too much sense, as you would expect more force to equal more jump height.
